AssessmentResult.description:
The full result of one assessment of one site against one reference.

``thresholds``, ``strata``, ``cases_to_review`` and ``site_name`` were added after the
first 0.1.0 files were written, so they are optional: an older file still validates,
and a reader shows "not recorded" rather than assuming defaults. ``check_descriptors``
(schemas 0.2.1) follows the same rule: a reader without it falls back to its own copy
of the default registry.

A site compared with its own reference data is visible from the two fingerprints
(:attr:`is_self_comparison`); it is derived, not stored, so it cannot disagree with them.

cases_to_review.description: Scans flagged for a human look; null when there are no scans.

check_descriptors.description: The descriptors (titles, definitions, sub-factors) of the check registry the run used, so a reader renders check cards from the result, not from its own copy. Null in files written before schemas 0.2.1; readers then fall back to the default registry.
check_descriptors.title: Check Descriptors

site_name.description: Human-readable site name for display, e.g. 'St. Mary's Hospital'. Never used as a key.
site_name.title: Site Name

strata.description: The by-group table; null when there are no scans.

thresholds.description: The resolved threshold profile the run used (same profile_id). Readers take group sizes, tolerances, markers and trigger lines from here, never from defaults.

AssessmentResult.title: AssessmentResult

Audience.description:
Who a check card is written for. INFERRED from ADR 0001 section 7 (decision
committee, clinicians, analysts); the POC has no such field.
Audience.title: Audience

BinMetricsV0.description:
Binary AAA-call metrics (``bin_metrics``, ipynb:835).

Count arithmetic is exact by construction in the notebook and is enforced:
``tp+fn == n_aaa``, ``tn+fp == n_not_aaa``, ``n_aaa+n_not_aaa == n``, and every no-answer
is counted as wrong, so ``n_no_answer <= fn+fp``. Rates are null exactly when their
denominator is 0, and ``*_lo <= point <= *_hi`` (95% Wilson).
BinMetricsV0.title: BinMetricsV0

CasesToReview.description:
Every flagged scan, most urgent first (priority, then the larger diameter error,
then case id). ``n_scans`` is how many scans were screened.
CasesToReview.title: CasesToReview

CheckDescriptor.description: What a check is, independent of any result. The UI renders cards from this.

legacy_check_key.description: The `check` value used in POC slicepoint.json findings.
legacy_check_key.title: Legacy Check Key

target.description: Default target score from the POC spec.
target.title: Target

CheckDescriptor.title: CheckDescriptor

CheckResult.description:
The outcome of one check for one assessment.

* ``status`` is primary.
* ``score`` (0-100) is optional; when present it must name ``score_method`` so a reader
  knows which formula produced it. No formula is agreed yet (ADR open question 2).
* ``n`` is required: the number of cases (scans) this check actually used, so thin
  evidence is visible. New checks must report their own per-check ``n`` (for example
  the cases with labels, or the AAA-positive cases for sensitivity). Only the legacy
  converter falls back to the file's scan count, because the POC never recorded it.
* ``n_effective`` (optional) is the effective sample size and must name
  ``n_effective_method`` (e.g. ``kish_design_effect_per_person``, ``cluster_icc``),
  mirroring score/score_method; ``0 < n_effective <= n``. Rationale: repeat scans of the
  same person (hospital_b has 80 scans from 40 real people) and clustering within a
  site are correlated, so they carry less information than ``n`` independent cases.
  That matters for Wilson intervals and for the "too few to judge" suppression, which
  should use the effective size, not the raw scan count.
* ``subjects`` (optional) is the number of distinct people behind the ``n`` cases, and
  ``subjects <= n``.
* ``failing_sub_factors`` must be sub-factors of the registered check, and must be empty
  when the status is ``ok``.

n.description: Cases this check actually used (per-check, not per-file).
n.title: N

CheckResult.title: CheckResult

CheckRun.description:
Whether a registered check ran. ``skipped`` means its required inputs were missing
(for example no labels or no embeddings); ``failed`` means it raised. Neither is ok.
CheckRun.title: CheckRun

CheckStatus.description: Categorical outcome of one check. Ordered ok < watch < problem.
CheckStatus.title: CheckStatus

datasets.description: Dataset folders under the data root (names only).

DiameterAgreement.description:
Bland-Altman style agreement of the model's diameter with the reference label.

``error = predicted - reference``. ``sd`` is the **population** SD of the error and
the 95% limits of agreement are ``bias +/- 1.96 sd``. Every float is null when
``n < min_n`` (3 in the POC). Tolerances are profile-driven, unlike the legacy
``DiameterMetricsV0`` whose ``within_2mm`` / ``within_3mm`` names fix them.
DiameterAgreement.title: DiameterAgreement

The binary-call and Dice blocks keep the POC shapes (``BinMetricsV0``,
``DiceMetricsV0``) and their arithmetic validators. The diameter block is the
profile-driven :class:`DiameterAgreement`; ``DiameterMetricsV0`` is for legacy files.

SliceThicknessClass.description:
Thickness class. In the data the mapping from ``slice_thickness_mm`` is exact:
thin < 2 mm (0.6-1.5 observed), standard 2.0-3.75, thick 5.0. The schema does not
enforce that mapping, because detecting inconsistent metadata is the analysis' job.
SliceThicknessClass.title: SliceThicknessClass

StepRecord.description: One step of the assessment pipeline. ``detail`` is required unless the step is ok.
StepRecord.title: StepRecord

Strata.description:
The by-group (stratified) table, computed by the runner. The suppression rules and
the size tolerance it used are recorded with it, so a reader never has to guess them.
Strata.title: Strata

StratumRow.description:
One group (``variable`` = ``level``) of the by-group table.

``too_few`` (fewer than ``Strata.min_group_size`` scans) suppresses every metric.
``sens_too_few`` (too few scans, or fewer than ``min_aaa_for_sensitivity``
aneurysms) suppresses sensitivity. Both rules count scans, not people. A missing
value of the variable is the level ``MISSING``.

within_tolerance.description: Share of the group's paired cases within Strata.size_tolerance_mm.
within_tolerance.title: Within Tolerance

StratumRow.title: StratumRow

ThresholdProfile.description:
All configurable numbers for one model (and optionally one site).

``check_targets`` keys are the checks this profile expects; a verdict treats any of
them that did not run as *not evaluated*. ``value_sources`` maps a dotted field path
(``aaa.decision_line_mm``, ``triggers.No-answer rate``) to a citation.

min_group_size.description: Minimum subgroup n for subgroup flags.
min_group_size.title: Min Group Size

parameters.description: Named numbers that are not yellow/red lines: similarity cut-offs, multipliers, grid bounds, plausible ranges, seeds. Keys are snake_case, no dots.
parameters.title: Parameters

ThresholdProfile.title: ThresholdProfile

TriggerKind.description: Display unit of a trigger value (history.csv ``kind``).
TriggerKind.title: TriggerKind

TriggerThreshold.description:
A yellow/red threshold pair with a direction.

Ordering must agree with ``worse``: for ``high`` red > yellow, for ``low`` red < yellow.
Comparisons are strict by default, as in ``monitor.evaluate``; ``inclusive=True`` makes
them ``>=`` / ``<=`` (the notebook uses that for domain AUC and the cutoff shift).

Either line may be absent, but not both. The notebook has red-only rules (repeats: any
near-duplicate share above 1% is red, with no yellow band) and yellow-only rules
(specificity below 0.90 is at most a watch).

inclusive.description: Compare with >= / <= instead of the strict > / <.
inclusive.title: Inclusive

TriggerThreshold.title: TriggerThreshold

Verdict.description:
A verdict with its rationale and the results it rests on.

Validated invariants (hold for any verdict, including a human override):

* ``go`` requires at least one result, every included result ``ok`` and nothing in
  ``not_evaluated``.
* ``no_go`` requires at least one ``problem``.
* check ids are unique and ``not_evaluated`` does not overlap the results.

These apply to the derived ``outcome``. ``override`` (optional) carries a human
decision. It must differ from the derived outcome, and :attr:`final_outcome` returns it.

not_evaluated.description: Checks the profile expects that produced no result.
not_evaluated.title: Not Evaluated

Verdict.title: Verdict

VerdictOverride.description:
A human decision that replaces the derived outcome.

Overriding to ``go`` while checks are ``problem`` or not evaluated is allowed, but only
through this record, so the departure from the rule is always attributed and justified.

by.description: Who made the decision (person or committee identifier).
by.title: By

note.description: Required justification, at least 20 characters after trimming whitespace.
note.title: Note

outcome.description: The final outcome, replacing the derived one.

VerdictOverride.title: VerdictOverride

WithinTolerance.description:
Share of cases with ``|predicted - reference| <= tolerance_mm``. The tolerance
comes from the threshold profile (``aaa.bland_altman_tolerance_mm`` /
``aaa.size_tolerance_mm``); ``share`` is null when there are too few pairs.
WithinTolerance.title: WithinTolerance

Worse.description: Which direction of a trigger value is bad.
Worse.title: Worse
